blocks.text: Madinah). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then came to Hadhrat Tameem (RA) saying, 'Go and see to that fire!' 'Who am I and what am I?' Hadhrat Tameem (RA) said. Hadhrat Umar (RA) however insisted until Hadhrat Tameem (RA) went with him. Hadhrat Mu'aawiya reports that he followed them as they proceeded to the fire where Hadhrat Tameem (RA) rounded up the fire with his bare hands until it returned into the crevice it had come out from, with Hadhrat Tameem (RA) behind it. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then remarked, 'The one who has witnessed this can never be like the one who has not (because it serves to boost one's Imaan).'"[^1]

Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Harmal says, "I once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have come to repent before being caught (for fighting by the side of Masaylama Kadhaab).' 'Who are you?' Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. 'I am Mu'aawiya bin Harmal, Musaylama's son-in-law,' I replied. He then said to me, 'Go and stay with the best person in Madinah.' I then went to stay with Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA). We were busy talking one day when a fire emerged from Harra. Hadhrat Umar (RA) came to Hadhrat Tameem (RA), saying, 'Go, O Tameem!' Humbling himself, Hadhrat Tameem (RA) said, 'Who am I? Are you not afraid that my inner self may become exposed?' He then got up and pushed the fire back through the door it came out from. He even went through the door behind it and later came out without the fire harming him in the least.[^2]
Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Tameem (RA), "It is for emergencies like this that we keep you hidden, O Abu Ruqayya."[^3]
Light Appears for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "We were once performing the Isha salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hasan (RA) and Husayn (RA) jumped on Rasulullaah ﷺ's back as he prostrated in Sajdah. When he got up from Sajdah, Rasulullaah ﷺ gently lowered them off his back but as soon as he went back into Sajdah, they again jumped on his back. When Rasulullaah ﷺ finally completed the salaah, he put them to sit on his lap. I then got up and offered, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Should I take them back home?' Just then a streak of lightning flashed and Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the two boys, 'You had better be going to your mother.' The light of the lightning then remained (to guide them home on that very dark night) until they entered their mother's house."[^4]
